mapping.caption: Mapping rules
mapping.empty: No rules yet. Add a rule to give members of a group access in Lunedo.
mapping.groupHint: Suggests the groups Lunedo has seen at sign-ins and synchronizations of {provider}, with their names where known. If a group is not listed yet, type its value exactly as {provider} sends it. Groups are matched by this value.
mapping.groupHintDirectory: Searches the groups of {provider} by name as you type and suggests the groups seen at sign-ins and synchronizations. Lunedo stores the ID of the group, so the rule keeps working when the group is renamed.
mapping.groupPlaceholder: Name or value of the group
mapping.noGroups: No group seen yet. Type the value of the group to use it.
mapping.noGroupsDirectory: No group with this name found. Check the spelling, or check that Lunedo may read groups in the directory.
mapping.useAsId: Use this text as group value
mapping.accounts: {count, plural, one {# account in Lunedo} other {# accounts in Lunedo}}
mapping.synchronizedGroup: Also add the members to a synchronized group in Lunedo
mapping.synchronizedGroupHint: The group is created with the name of the provider group and can only be changed in the provider.
mapping.makeHome: Make this organization the home organization
mapping.makeHomeHint: Only needed when rules lead into several organizations. Otherwise the first organization an account joins becomes its home organization. When several rules name a home organization, the first rule in the list decides.
mapping.instanceRoleNote: Instance roles never grant access to the content of organizations. Groups of organizations in Lunedo can never receive them.
mapping.previewOrganization: {count, plural, one {# person becomes a member of {organization}.} other {# people become members of {organization}.}}
mapping.previewInstance: {count, plural, one {# person receives the instance role {role}.} other {# people receive the instance role {role}.}}
mapping.previewAccounts: {count, plural, one {# of them has an account already.} other {# of them have an account already.}}
mapping.previewSplit: {accounts} of them have an account already, {later} get one at their next sign-in.
mapping.removeDescription: Members of {name} lose what this rule granted at their next sign-in or sync. Access granted by hand stays.
mapping.hint: Rules apply at every sign-in and sync. Removing someone from the group in {provider} removes what the rule granted. Groups created by rules are read-only in Lunedo.
mapping.byNameTitle: Groups are identified by their names
mapping.byName: {provider} sends group names, not identifiers. Renaming a group in {provider} breaks every rule for it until the rule is changed here.
mapping.chooseGroup: Choose the group whose members the rule applies to.
mapping.chooseOrganization: Choose the organization the rule gives access to.

sync.started: Synchronization started. Results appear here in about a minute.

signInOnly.generic: Profile and groups of this provider update at every sign-in. It has no directory Lunedo could synchronize with in the background; with a SCIM connection, the provider sends changes at once.
signInOnly.google: Google Workspace is only used to sign in. Turn on group synchronization in the settings to read groups and synchronize them in the background.
signInOnly.entraId: This provider is only read at sign-in.
signInOnly.saml: Profile and groups of this provider update at every sign-in. SAML has no directory Lunedo could synchronize with in the background.
signInOnly.ldap: This directory is only read at sign-in.

sync.caption: Synchronization runs
sync.cancelledSummary: Stopped on request. Changes made until then stay.
sync.cancelRequested: The run stops before the next account.
sync.alreadyEnded: This run has already ended. The sync log shows its result.
sync.failedWithoutReason: The run failed without a reason. Check the connection and try again.
sync.heldDescription: The run would have deactivated {count, plural, one {# account} other {# accounts}} at once and stopped without deactivating anyone. A wrong search base, a moved directory unit or missing read permissions look the same as people leaving. Check the provider first; if the people really left, confirm the run.
sync.heldConfirmed: An administrator confirmed the deactivation of up to {count, plural, one {# account} other {# accounts}} on {time}.
sync.confirmDescription: A new run starts and may deactivate up to {count, plural, one {# account} other {# accounts}}. Their sessions end and their personal API tokens are revoked. Accounts come back when they are enabled in the provider again; revoked tokens do not.
sync.intervalHint: Groups and account status are also updated at every sign-in.
sync.deactivationLimitHint: Protects against deactivating many accounts by mistake. If one run would deactivate more of this provider's accounts than this share, and more than the minimum below, it stops and changes nobody. The instance administrators are told and can confirm the run in the sync log.
sync.deactivationMinimum: Accounts a run may always deactivate
sync.deactivationMinimumHint: A run stops only when it would deactivate more than this number of accounts as well as more than the share above. A run that finds none of the linked accounts always stops.
sync.whenDisabledHint: Accounts disabled or deleted in {provider} are deactivated in Lunedo and reactivated when enabled again. Lunedo never deletes accounts.
sync.groupSyncHint: Without it, Google Workspace is only used to sign in, and mapping rules see no groups.
sync.adminRoleSetup: In the Google Admin console, assign the prebuilt role Groups Reader to the service account under Account > Admin roles. Lunedo then reads groups as the service account itself, without acting for a person.
sync.delegationWarning: With domain-wide delegation the service account acts as the administrator below and may use everything its scopes allow for the whole domain. Prefer the administrator role unless your setup requires delegation.
sync.readUsersHint: Needs a role that can also read users, for example a custom role with Users > Read. Without it, Lunedo does not see suspensions: a suspended person can no longer sign in through Google, but open sessions run until they expire.
sync.adminEmailHint: The service account acts on behalf of this administrator through domain-wide delegation.
sync.keyPlaceholder: Paste the JSON key of the service account
sync.keyRequired: Paste the JSON key of the service account.

identityProviders.description: How people sign in to this instance.
identityProviders.removeDescription: Removes the provider, its rules and all identities linked through it. To stop sign-ins for a while, deactivate it instead.
identityProviders.removeConfirm: This cannot be undone. Accounts and their content stay.

removal.accounts: {count, plural, =0 {No account is linked to this provider.} one {# account loses its identity of this provider.} other {# accounts lose their identity of this provider.}}

secondFactor.title: Second factor
secondFactor.mode: Second factor after a sign-in through this provider

modes.lunedo: Always ask for a Lunedo second factor

hints.provider: A sign-in through this provider is complete. Set up multi-factor authentication in the provider.
hints.providerProof: The provider must report multi-factor authentication in its sign-in token. Without it, Lunedo asks for its own second factor; people without one set one up first.
hints.lunedo: After every sign-in through this provider, Lunedo asks for its own second factor; people without one set one up first.

secondFactor.proofValuesHint: Values of the amr claim that count as multi-factor authentication, separated by commas. Most providers send mfa.
secondFactor.proofValuesInvalid: Enter 1 to 20 values of up to 50 characters, separated by commas.

directoryModes.lunedo: Always ask for a Lunedo second factor

directoryHints.lunedo: A directory password proves no second factor. After every sign-in with it, Lunedo asks for its own second factor; people without one set one up first.
directoryHints.provider: A directory password proves no second factor. Lunedo still asks for one where the instance or an organization requires it.

status.title: Status
status.deactivatedNotice: Nobody can sign in through it and it is not synchronized. Its settings, rules and groups stay. Activate it again in the settings.
status.deactivateDescription: Stops sign-ins and synchronization through this provider and ends the sessions that came from it. Settings, rules and groups stay, and you can activate it again.
status.deactivateConfirm: Nobody can sign in through this provider any more, and the sessions that came from it end now. Ended sessions do not come back when you activate the provider again; people have to sign in anew. Settings, rules, groups and access stay.
status.activateDescription: People can sign in through this provider again, and synchronization continues.

identityProviders.emptyDescription: Add Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace or another OIDC provider, so people sign in with their work account.
identityProviders.domainHint: The sign-in page chooses the provider by the domain of the e-mail address or sign-in name people enter.
identityProviders.noPermission: Your roles do not allow you to change identity providers.

warnings.expiringAction: Create a new credential at the provider and add it here before then, or sign-in through this provider stops working.
warnings.stoppedAction: Add a valid credential from the provider, then test the sign-in.
warnings.metadataTitle: The metadata of {name} could not be refreshed
warnings.metadataRefreshFailed: Metadata of {name} could not be refreshed at {time}: {error}. Lunedo keeps using the last good metadata. Check the metadata address or upload the file again.
warnings.caExpiring: The CA certificate of {name} expires on {date}
warnings.caExpiringAction: Upload the new CA certificate of the directory in the provider's connection settings before then, or Lunedo can no longer connect to the directory.
warnings.noGraphTitle: {name} cannot read groups through Microsoft Graph
warnings.noGraph: Entra ID leaves out the groups of people in more than 150 groups. Without access to Microsoft Graph, these accounts lose their groups and the access the rules give. Add the client ID of an app registration and its credential.

overview.rulesHint: Groups that grant access in Lunedo.
overview.missingGroups: {count, plural, one {# rule points to a group that no longer exists} other {# rules point to groups that no longer exist}}

identityProviders.redirectUriHint: Enter this address in the app registration of your provider.

fields.name: Name on the sign-in page

nameHints.entraId: For example Microsoft or the name of your company.
nameHints.google: For example Google or the name of your company.
nameHints.oidc: For example Keycloak or the name of your company.
nameHints.saml: For example ADFS or the name of your company.
nameHints.ldap: For example Active Directory or the name of your company.

fields.tenantIdHint: Found in the overview of your Entra ID tenant.
fields.tenantIdInvalid: Enter the tenant ID as shown in Entra ID, for example 3f2a9c1e-7b4d-4e8a-9c21-5d6f0a8b2e17.
fields.issuerHint: The address of the provider. Lunedo reads its configuration from /.well-known/openid-configuration.
fields.googleDomains: Enter at least one Google Workspace domain.
fields.algorithmHint: The only algorithm Lunedo accepts for ID tokens from this provider.

attributes.description: Lunedo recognizes an account by the provider's identifier, never by its e-mail address. The other attributes fill the profile and update at every sign-in.
attributes.identifierHint: Never changes, also when names or addresses change.
attributes.fixed: Fixed for this type of provider
attributes.emailHint: Used for notifications, invitations and the home organization by domain.
attributes.signInNameHint: Shown next to the e-mail address, so people recognize their work account.
attributes.googleFixed: Google Workspace sends the e-mail address, name and user ID; there is nothing to choose.

claims.groupsHint: Leave empty if the provider does not send groups.
claims.groupNamesHint: Optional. Groups are matched by their ID; names are only shown.

saml.identifierHint: An attribute that never changes for a person, such as objectGUID.
saml.identifierHintGeneric: Leave empty to use the persistent NameID of the identity provider.
saml.optionalHint: Optional. Leave empty if the identity provider does not send it.

groupValuesHint.adfs: In the claim rules of the relying party trust, send Token-Groups as SIDs. SIDs stay the same when a group is renamed.
groupValuesHint.generic: What the groups attribute contains. Identifiers stay the same when a group is renamed.

saml.namesWarning: With group names, renaming a group in the provider breaks the rules for it. Use identifiers if the provider can send them.

accounts.createHint: Without this, only invited people and existing accounts can sign in.
accounts.domainsHint: Enter every domain your people use at this provider, for sign-in names and for e-mail addresses, for example example.com and example.at. The sign-in page sends people with these domains to this provider, e-mail addresses in them count as confirmed, and accounts are created only for them. A domain belongs to one provider only.
accounts.domainsHintEntraId: Enter every domain that is verified in the tenant, for sign-in names and for e-mail addresses, for example example.com and example.at. The sign-in page sends people with these domains to this provider, e-mail addresses in them count as confirmed, and accounts are created only for them. A domain belongs to one provider only.
accounts.domainsHintGoogle: Enter every domain of your Google Workspace, for sign-in names and for e-mail addresses. The sign-in page sends people with these domains to Google.
accounts.domainsInvalid: Enter domains like example.org, separated by commas.
accounts.requireGroupHint: Usually not needed: restrict access in the provider instead. Use this only when the provider cannot restrict access itself.
accounts.groupsHint: IDs of the groups at the provider, separated by commas. Membership in one of them is enough.
accounts.linkHint: When an account with the same verified address exists, the person confirms once with its password and second factor. Lunedo never links accounts automatically.
accounts.domainsHintDirectory: Enter the domains of the e-mail addresses and sign-in names in the directory, for example example.com. The sign-in page asks people with these domains for their directory password, and accounts are created only for them. A domain belongs to one provider only.

credentials.title: Credentials
credentials.expiresOnHint: Lunedo reminds you 30 and 7 days before.
credentials.certificateHint: Lunedo creates a key pair. Upload the certificate to the app registration; the private key never leaves Lunedo.
credentials.certificateUpload: Download the certificate and upload it to the app registration at your provider.
credentials.removeDescription: Lunedo stops using it at once. Make sure a newer credential works first.
credentials.bindPasswordHint: Lunedo stores it encrypted and uses it only to search the directory.
credentials.signingHint: Lunedo creates a new key pair for signing its requests. Its metadata lists the new certificate at once.
credentials.signingUpload: Lunedo's metadata contains the new certificate. Let the identity provider load the metadata again, or download the certificate and add it there. Remove the old certificate once the identity provider uses the new one.

addDescriptions.oidc: The current credential keeps working until you remove it, so you can switch without interruption.
addDescriptions.saml: The current certificate keeps working until you remove it, so the identity provider can switch without interruption.
addDescriptions.ldap: Change the password of the service account in the directory first, then enter it here. Remove the old one afterwards.
addDescriptions.graph: The current credential for Microsoft Graph keeps working until you remove it, so you can switch without interruption.

noneDescriptions.oidc: Sign-in through this provider does not work until you add a client secret or a certificate.
noneDescriptions.saml: Lunedo cannot sign its requests until you add a signing certificate.
noneDescriptions.ldap: Lunedo cannot search the directory until you enter the password of the service account.

renewHints.oidc: During a renewal, old and new credential both work. Remove the old one once the new one is in place.
renewHints.saml: During a renewal, Lunedo's metadata lists old and new certificate. Remove the old one once the identity provider uses the new one.
renewHints.ldap: The password has no expiry date in Lunedo. To rotate it, enter the new password and remove the old one.
renewHints.graph: During a renewal, old and new credential both work. Remove the old one once the new one is in place.

credentials.removeLast: Lunedo uses it now and has no other. Sign-in through {name} stops until you add a new one.
credentials.removeInUse: Lunedo uses it now and switches to another credential of the same kind.
credentials.removeUnused: Not in use. Removing it does not change how people sign in.

logo.label: Logo
logo.hint: Shown on the sign-in button. PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 256 KiB. Microsoft and Google use their own buttons.
logo.removeDescription: The sign-in button shows a key icon instead.

test.title: Test the connection
test.description: Sign in once with a test account. Nothing is saved, and no account is created.
test.unreachable: Lunedo could not reach {provider} to start the test. Check the connection settings of this provider, then test again.
test.summary: Received {claims, plural, one {# claim} other {# claims}} and {groups, plural, one {# group} other {# groups}}.
test.unverifiedTitle: The e-mail address is not in the provider's domains
test.unverified: {email} is not in one of the configured domains. Lunedo does not link or create accounts for it.
test.subject: Identifier
test.noClaims: The provider sent no claims or attributes.
test.claimsHint: Tokens, hashes and secrets are never shown.

failures.providerRefused: {provider} refused the sign-in. Check the message above, correct the setting at {provider} or in Lunedo, then start the test again.
failures.userNotAssigned: The test account is not assigned to the application. Assign the person or one of their groups to the enterprise application at {provider}, or turn off the assignment requirement, then test again.
failures.consentRequired: The application has no consent for the requested permissions. Grant admin consent for the app registration at {provider}, then test again.
failures.unknownApplication: {provider} does not know the client ID. Copy the application (client) ID of the app registration into Lunedo, then test again.
failures.invalidClient: {provider} did not accept any credential of Lunedo. Add the current client secret or upload Lunedo's certificate at {provider}, then test again.
failures.otherTenant: The test account belongs to another tenant than the one set in Lunedo. Check the tenant ID, or sign in with an account of the configured tenant.
failures.domainNotAllowed: The account is not in one of the provider's domains. Add its domain to the provider, or test with an account of a configured domain.
failures.browserChanged: The sign-in came back in another browser, or the browser lost Lunedo's cookie on the way. Start the test again in this browser and finish it at {provider} without switching browsers.
failures.invalidResponse: Lunedo could not accept the answer of {provider}. Check the message above and the settings at {provider}, such as the redirect URI and the signing certificate, then test again.

test.noEmailTitle: The provider sent no e-mail address
test.noEmailEntraId: Without an address, Lunedo cannot create or link an account. Choose User principal name as the source of the e-mail address under User attributes, or set the e-mail address of the person in {provider}.
test.noEmail: Without an address, Lunedo cannot create or link an account. Set the e-mail address of the person in {provider}, or choose the claim or attribute that carries it under User attributes.

check.failedTitle: Lunedo could not reach the provider with these settings
check.passwordNeeded: Lunedo uses the stored password only for the server it belongs to. Enter the password of the service account to connect to this server.
check.serverPasswordHint: Lunedo connects to the new server with it before saving. To store another password, replace it under Credentials.
check.saveAnywayHint: Correct the marked field, or save anyway and correct it later. The setup can then only be finished after you confirm the failed check.
check.finishDescription: Lunedo checked {check} again and it failed: {message} People cannot sign in through this provider until this works.

discovery.status: {status} at {url}. Check the issuer: Lunedo adds /.well-known/openid-configuration to it.
discovery.unreachable: No answer from {url}. Check the issuer for typing errors and that this server can reach the provider.
discovery.invalidDocument: {url} did not return an OpenID Connect discovery document. Check the issuer.
discovery.issuerMismatch: The document at {url} names the issuer {detail}. Enter exactly this issuer.

metadata.unreachable: No answer from {url}. Check the metadata address and that this server can reach it.
metadata.invalidDocument: {url} did not return usable SAML metadata: {detail}

directory.connection: Lunedo could not connect to {url}: {detail} Check the server address and the port, and that this server can reach the directory.
directory.certificate: The certificate of {url} is not trusted: {detail} Choose the CA certificate of the directory, or check the server name.
directory.serviceAccount: The directory did not accept the service account: {detail} Check its name and password.
directory.search: Nobody was found under the base DN for people: {detail} Check the base DN.

wizard.title: Add identity provider

entraId.title: Microsoft Entra ID
entraId.hint: OIDC with groups through Microsoft Graph.
entraId.capabilities: Groups and account status are synchronized in the background; disabled accounts are deactivated.

google.title: Google Workspace
google.hint: OIDC with groups through the Directory API.
google.capabilities: Sign-in only at first. Group synchronization can be turned on later with a service account.

oidc.title: Other OIDC provider
oidc.hint: Keycloak, Authentik, Okta, Zitadel and others.
oidc.capabilities: Profile and groups update at every sign-in. There is no background synchronization.

saml.title: SAML 2.0
saml.hint: ADFS, Shibboleth or Entra ID through SAML.
saml.capabilities: Profile and groups update at every sign-in. With Entra ID, groups can also be synchronized through Microsoft Graph.

ldap.title: LDAP or Active Directory
ldap.hint: Sign-in with directory passwords and group sync.
ldap.capabilities: Groups and account status are synchronized in the background; disabled accounts are deactivated.

savedHints.oidc: Lunedo knows how to reach the provider now. Choose below which values it reads, then test the sign-in.
savedHints.saml: Lunedo has read the metadata of the identity provider. Choose below which attributes it reads, then test the sign-in.
savedHints.ldap: Lunedo reaches the directory with the service account. Choose below how people sign in.

metadataUrlHints.entraId: The App Federation Metadata URL from the SAML settings of the enterprise application.
metadataUrlHints.generic: The address of the identity provider's metadata, starting with https://.

wizard.metadataFileHint: The XML file with the metadata of the identity provider. Without an address, upload a new file whenever its certificate changes.
wizard.metadataFileRequired: Choose the metadata file of the identity provider.
wizard.fileUnreadable: The file could not be read. Choose it again or try another file.

ldapHints.activeDirectory: Create a service account in Active Directory that may read people and groups. It needs no other rights.
ldapHints.generic: Create a service account in the directory that may read people and groups, for example in OpenLDAP or FreeIPA. It needs no other rights.

wizard.caHint: Optional. Only needed when the server certificate was issued by your own certificate authority.
wizard.caFailedTitle: The provider is saved, but the CA certificate is not
wizard.caFailedAction: Continue and upload the right CA certificate in the test step or in the connection settings.
wizard.graphHint: SAML assertions from Entra ID carry at most 150 groups. With an app registration that has the application permissions GroupMember.Read.All and User.Read.All, Lunedo loads the rest through Microsoft Graph and also synchronizes accounts in the background. You can skip this step and add it later in the settings.
wizard.draftHint: Lunedo saves the setup as a draft from the next step on. You can close the assistant and continue later from the list of identity providers.
wizard.draftNotSaved: Your last changes could not be saved to the draft. Check the connection; Lunedo tries again with your next change.
wizard.copyHint: Register Lunedo {place} with these values first. They do not change, so you can copy them now and fill in the fields further down afterwards.

registerHints.entraId: Create an app registration with the redirect URI below. Under Enterprise applications, turn on Assignment required and assign the groups that may use Lunedo.
registerHints.google: Create an OAuth client of type Web application with the redirect URI below.
registerHints.oidc: Create a confidential OIDC client with the redirect URI below.
registerHints.samlEntraId: Create an enterprise application with SAML single sign-on and enter the entity ID and the reply URL below.
registerHints.adfs: Add a relying party trust that reads Lunedo's metadata address below.
registerHints.saml: Create a SAML service provider with the entity ID and the assertion consumer service URL below, or let it read Lunedo's metadata.

wizard.signingCertificateHint: Upload it {place} if signed requests are checked there. It is also part of Lunedo's metadata.

places.entraId: in the Microsoft Entra admin center

wizard.typeFixed: Fixed once the provider is saved
wizard.stepLater: Opens after the current step is saved

saml.entityIdHint: Also called identifier or audience at the identity provider.
saml.acsUrlHint: Also called reply URL. The identity provider sends the sign-in response to this address.
saml.metadataUrlHint: Most identity providers can read this address or the downloaded file, so you do not have to enter the values above by hand.
saml.noMetadataUrl: Lunedo could not load the metadata yet, so nobody can sign in. Check the metadata address and load it again.
saml.noMetadataFile: Upload the metadata file of the identity provider. Nobody can sign in until then.
saml.refreshFailedTitle: The metadata could not be refreshed
saml.sourceHint: With an address, Lunedo loads the metadata again every day and picks up new certificates of the identity provider by itself.
saml.metadataAddressHint: The address of the identity provider's metadata, starting with https://.
saml.idpEntityId: Entity ID of the identity provider
saml.certificatesHint: Lunedo accepts only responses signed with one of these certificates.
saml.idpInitiated: Allow sign-in started at the identity provider
saml.idpInitiatedHint: Sign-in started at the identity provider cannot be tied to a request from this browser, so an attacker could sign someone into the attacker's account. Turn it on only if people must start from a portal such as the Microsoft app launcher.
saml.requireSignedResponseHint: The assertion must always be signed. Entra ID and ADFS sign only the assertion by default; turn this on only if your identity provider also signs the whole response.
saml.encryptedAssertionsHint: The identity provider encrypts the assertion with Lunedo's certificate from the metadata. Turn it on only after the identity provider is set up for it, or sign-in stops working.
saml.graphClientIdHint: Optional. With an app registration and a credential for it, Lunedo reads groups beyond the token limit and synchronizes the directory through Microsoft Graph.

ldap.urlHint: The address of your directory server, for example ldaps://dc01.example.org. A server name alone, such as dc01.example.org, is enough; Lunedo then uses ldaps:// on port 636. Plain ldap:// works only with StartTLS, so passwords are never sent unencrypted.
ldap.urlInvalid: Enter an address such as ldaps://dc01.example.org, without a path.
ldap.urlInvalidStartTls: Enter an ldap:// address while StartTLS is on. To use ldaps://, turn StartTLS off first.
ldap.startTlsHint: Encrypts the ldap:// connection before any password is sent.
ldap.startTlsLdaps: Only for ldap:// addresses; ldaps:// is encrypted already.
ldap.plainWarning: Without StartTLS, passwords travel unencrypted. Lunedo refuses such a connection unless the instance runs with insecure identity providers allowed.
ldap.bindDnHint: The account Lunedo uses to look people up, for example CN=lunedo,OU=Service,DC=example,DC=org. It only needs to read people and groups.
ldap.bindDnHintActiveDirectory: The account Lunedo uses to look people up, for example svc-lunedo@example.org. EXAMPLE\svc-lunedo or the full distinguished name work as well. It only needs to read people and groups.
ldap.userBaseDnHint: The part of the directory that holds the people who may sign in, for example OU=Staff,DC=example,DC=org. Lunedo also looks in everything below it.
ldap.groupBaseDnHint: The part of the directory that holds the groups, for example OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=org. Lunedo also looks in everything below it.
ldap.dnInvalid: Enter a distinguished name such as OU=Staff,DC=example,DC=org.
ldap.serviceAccountInvalid: Enter a distinguished name, a user principal name such as svc-lunedo@example.org, or EXAMPLE\svc-lunedo.
ldap.userFilterHint: Which entries count as people who can sign in, for example (objectClass=person). The suggested value fits most directories.
ldap.groupFilterHint: Which entries count as groups, for example (objectClass=group). The suggested value fits most directories.
ldap.filterInvalid: Enter an LDAP filter in parentheses, such as (objectClass=person).
ldap.signInAttributeHint: What people enter on the sign-in page besides their password.
ldap.attributeInvalid: Enter an LDAP attribute name such as mail.
ldap.testPersonHint: Sign-in name of a person in the directory. Lunedo reads every attribute the directory returns for this person, so you can choose from them below.
ldap.attributesRead: {count, plural, one {The directory returned # attribute for {person}.} other {The directory returned # attributes for {person}.}}
ldap.attributesReadFirst: {count, plural, one {No test person was entered, so Lunedo read the first person the directory returned: {person}, with # attribute.} other {No test person was entered, so Lunedo read the first person the directory returned: {person}, with # attributes.}}
ldap.noMatchAddress: {attribute} holds an address such as lena@example.org. Enter the full address, or choose another attribute under Sign-in name.
ldap.noMatchOther: If people sign in with another value, choose it under Sign-in name. Otherwise check the base DN and the filter for people.
ldap.attributeChoiceHint: Read the attributes of a test person to choose from every attribute the directory returns.
ldap.attributeNotReturned: The directory returned no value of this attribute for the test person. Choose another attribute or check the person in the directory.
ldap.groupMembershipHint: Where the directory records who belongs to a group.
ldap.disabledAttributeHint: Optional. Leave empty if the directory does not mark disabled accounts.
ldap.disabledValuesHint: Separated by commas. Without values, any value of the attribute means disabled.
ldap.disabledValuesInvalid: Enter up to 20 values of up to 256 characters, separated by commas.
ldap.caDescription: Needed when the server certificate of the directory was issued by your own certificate authority.
ldap.caNoneHint: Lunedo trusts only certificates of public certificate authorities.

scim.intro: With SCIM, the provider sends changes of people and groups to Lunedo at once instead of waiting for the next sign-in or synchronization. Accounts are created before the first sign-in and deactivated, never deleted.
scim.accounts: Everyone assigned to the app at the provider gets an account, even when account creation at first sign-in is off.
scim.entraSetup: Entra ID needs P1 or higher. In the enterprise application, open Provisioning, choose Automatic, enter the URL below as tenant URL and the token as secret token. Then change the attribute mappings for users as shown below.
scim.entraMappingsHint: In the enterprise application, open Provisioning, Mappings, Provision Microsoft Entra ID Users and edit the attribute in the first column. Groups keep their default mapping.
scim.mappingExternalIdWhen: Always. Entra ID sends mailNickname by default, but Lunedo identifies people by their object ID, as at sign-in.
scim.mappingEmailWhen: When accounts have no mailbox. Entra ID sends mail by default, which is empty without a mailbox, and Lunedo needs an e-mail address.
scim.genericSetup: Enter the URL below and the token as bearer token at your provider. externalId must carry the identifier the provider uses at sign-in.
scim.urlHint: The SCIM endpoint of this provider.

scim.noRequests: No request yet. Test the connection at the provider.
scim.leads: While SCIM is on, it leads: the background synchronization of this provider runs once a day as a reconciliation. The sync log shows SCIM requests with their changes and errors.
scim.onlyOnce: Copy the token now and enter it at the provider. Lunedo shows it only this once.
scim.overlap: The previous token keeps working for seven days, so the provider is not interrupted while you change it.
scim.removeDescription: Requests with this token are refused at once.
scim.removeLast: Requests with this token are refused at once. Without a token, SCIM is off and the background synchronization returns to its interval.

apiTokens_requestsPerMinute.description: Per minute. Further requests are refused for a moment.

apiTokens_expiryReminderDays.label: Expiry reminder
apiTokens_expiryReminderDays.description: Owners are reminded this long before a token expires.

apiTokens_publicDocumentation.label: Public API reference
apiTokens_publicDocumentation.description: Everyone can open the API reference, also without signing in.

organizations_selfServiceCreation.label: Self-service organizations
organizations_selfServiceCreation.description: Every member may create organizations, which they then own.

organizations_membersCreateGroups.label: Members create groups
organizations_membersCreateGroups.description: Members may create groups and manage them.

organizations_selfRegistration.label: Self-registration
organizations_selfRegistration.description: People with an address in one of the domains can create an account themselves.

organizations_guestExpiryReminderDays.label: Guest expiry reminder
organizations_guestExpiryReminderDays.description: The responsible person is reminded this long before a guest's access ends.

organizations_guestInactivityDays.label: Inactive guests
organizations_guestInactivityDays.description: The responsible person is told when a guest has not been active for this long.

organizations_expiryReminderDays.label: Access expiry reminder
organizations_expiryReminderDays.description: The people responsible are reminded this long before roles and memberships expire.

apiTokens_unusedNoticeDays.label: Unused API tokens
apiTokens_unusedNoticeDays.description: Notify the owner when a token has not been used for this long. The token keeps working.

spaces_membersCreateSpaces.label: Members create spaces
spaces_membersCreateSpaces.description: Members may create spaces. Administrators always can; guests and collaborators never.

spaces_personalSpaces.label: Personal spaces
spaces_personalSpaces.description: Every person with a standard account gets a personal space when they first open it.

appearance_folderView.label: Folder view
appearance_folderView.description: Show the contents of folders as a list or as tiles.

pages_defaultMode.label: Default mode of new pages
pages_defaultMode.description: In publish mode, readers see the last published version while editors work on a draft. In live mode, readers see every change at once. Each page can deviate.

pages_liveVersionIdleMinutes.label: Version after a pause in live mode
pages_liveVersionIdleMinutes.description: A page in live mode gets a version after this time without changes, or when the last person editing leaves.

pages_status.label: Page status
pages_status.description: Editors can mark how far a page is, and readers see it at the top of the page. Turning it off hides the status everywhere; pages keep it in case you turn it on again.

trash_firstStageDays.label: Time in the trash
trash_firstStageDays.description: How long editors can restore deleted pages from the trash of a space.

trash_secondStageDays.label: Time in second-stage recovery
trash_secondStageDays.description: After the trash, only organization administrators can restore content for this long. Then it is deleted for good.

trash_firstStageMinimumDays.label: Shortest time in the trash
trash_firstStageMinimumDays.description: Organizations and spaces cannot set a shorter time in the trash.

trash_secondStageMinimumDays.label: Shortest time in second-stage recovery
trash_secondStageMinimumDays.description: Organizations and spaces cannot set a shorter time in second-stage recovery.

reactions_enabled.label: Reactions
reactions_enabled.description: People can react with emoji to pages, blog posts and comments.

files_maxFileSizeMegabytes.label: Largest file to upload
files_maxFileSizeMegabytes.description: Uploads above this size are refused before anything is stored, with a message that names the limit. Organizations can only lower it.

files_keepVersions.label: Versions of a file to keep
files_keepVersions.description: When a new version is uploaded and there are more than this number, the oldest version not marked to keep is removed. Marked versions and versions that a page version still shows, such as drawings, are always kept and do not count.

sharing_shareLinks.label: Share links
sharing_shareLinks.description: People who may share a page can create links for named people, the organization or everyone signed in.

sharing_anyoneLinks.label: Links for anyone without signing in
sharing_anyoneLinks.description: Visitors see only the shared page. Each link needs an expiry date. Restricted pages never get such links.

sharing_anyoneLinkMaxDays.label: Longest lifetime of a link for anyone
sharing_anyoneLinkMaxDays.description: Links for anyone must expire within this time. Organizations can only shorten it.

sharing_membersInviteGuests.label: Members can invite guests to a page
sharing_membersInviteGuests.description: When on, people who may share a page can invite someone by e-mail as a guest. Administrators of the organization can always do this.

files_keepVersionsMaximum.label: Most versions organizations and spaces may keep
files_keepVersionsMaximum.description: Organizations and spaces can choose any number up to this maximum. Only here can it be set to no limit.

spaces_membersCreateConfidentialSpaces.label: Members create confidential spaces
spaces_membersCreateConfidentialSpaces.description: Members may create confidential spaces and one-on-ones that administrators cannot read. Administrators always can.

imports_maxUploadMegabytes.label: Largest export to upload
imports_maxUploadMegabytes.description: Exports above this size are refused before the upload starts, with a hint to raise this limit or to use the organization's import folder on the server.

imports_maxOrganizationMegabytes.label: Import storage per organization
imports_maxOrganizationMegabytes.description: Uploaded exports and the data Lunedo reads from them count together for each organization. When an organization reaches this limit, new uploads and reading are refused until earlier imports are finished, discarded or deleted.

imports_folderEnabled.label: Import folder
imports_folderEnabled.description: Organization administrators can import exports placed in their organization's subfolder of the import folder, named after the organization's ID. Files at the top level or in another organization's subfolder are never offered.

imports_atlassianHosts.label: Further Atlassian sites
imports_atlassianHosts.description: Host names Lunedo may contact with an import's API token besides sites under atlassian.net, separated by commas, such as wiki.example.com.

spaces_export.label: Allow export
spaces_export.description: People can export pages and the space as PDF, Word, HTML and Markdown. When it is off, nobody can export, space admins included.

content_language.label: Content language
content_language.description: Language of the pages in this space. Search uses it to find words in all their forms, for example houses when someone searches for house. Each page can use a different language.

notifications_digestTime.label: Send the digest at
notifications_digestTime.description: In each person's own time zone. Only sent when something happened.

notifications_watchAutomatically.label: Watch what I create, edit or comment on
notifications_watchAutomatically.description: You get changes and comments on these items.

notifications_browserPush.label: Browser push
notifications_browserPush.description: Lets people receive notifications through the push services of browser makers.

notifications_digestEnabled.label: Send a daily summary by e-mail
notifications_digestEnabled.description: Collects the notifications whose e-mail is set to the daily summary. Turned off, they appear only in the app.

storage_reminder.label: Reminder while a level is active
storage_reminder.description: How often Lunedo repeats the current state to the people who were told, while a warning level stays active.

operations_updateCheck.label: Check for updates
operations_updateCheck.description: Downloads the public version file once a day and tells instance administrators about new versions. Off: Lunedo makes no request for it.

unknown.what: The export could not be read
unknown.action: Try again. If it happens again, ask the person who runs the server to check the logs.

notAnArchive.what: The file is not a ZIP archive
notAnArchive.cause: Confluence exports spaces as ZIP files. The file may be damaged or incomplete.
notAnArchive.action: Export the space again and upload the ZIP file.

wrongFormat.what: The file has the other export format
wrongFormat.cause: The chosen format does not match the file.
wrongFormat.action: Choose the other export format above; the file is read again.

notConfluenceExport.what: The file is not a Confluence space export
notConfluenceExport.cause: The archive contains none of the files of a Confluence export.
notConfluenceExport.action: In Confluence open the space, then Space settings › Export space, and upload that file.

notSpaceExport.what: The file is neither a space export nor a site backup
notSpaceExport.cause: Lunedo reads XML and CSV space exports and XML site backups of Confluence.
notSpaceExport.action: Export a single space or create a site backup in Confluence and upload that file.

spaceChoiceRequired.what: The site backup contains several spaces
spaceChoiceRequired.cause: A site backup holds every space of the Confluence site, and an import takes one of them.
spaceChoiceRequired.action: Choose the space in the step Source.

archiveTooLarge.what: The archive expands to more than allowed
archiveTooLarge.cause: Its content is larger than the limits for imports. Real exports stay below them; the file may be crafted.
archiveTooLarge.action: Export the space again. If it is really that large, split it into several spaces.

tooManyEntries.what: The archive contains too many files
tooManyEntries.cause: It has more files than the limit for imports.
tooManyEntries.action: Export the space again, or split it into several spaces.

compressionRatio.what: A file in the archive is compressed too strongly
compressionRatio.cause: Real exports are never compressed this much; the file may be crafted to fill the server.
compressionRatio.action: Export the space again from Confluence.

unsafeEntryName.what: The archive contains unsafe file names
unsafeEntryName.cause: A name points outside the archive, has a drive letter or is a symbolic link. Confluence never creates such names.
unsafeEntryName.action: Export the space again from Confluence and do not change the archive.

encryptedEntry.action: Upload the export as Confluence created it, without a password.

unsupportedCompression.what: The archive uses an unknown compression
unsupportedCompression.cause: The archive was probably repacked with another tool.
unsupportedCompression.action: Upload the export as Confluence created it.

xmlDeclaration.what: The export contains document type declarations
xmlDeclaration.cause: Confluence exports contain none; such declarations can be used to attack the server.
xmlDeclaration.action: Export the space again from Confluence.

xmlTooDeep.what: The export nests its content too deeply
xmlTooDeep.cause: The structure is deeper than the limit for imports.
xmlTooDeep.action: Export the space again from Confluence.

xmlElementTooLarge.what: The export contains an entry that is too large
xmlElementTooLarge.cause: One entry, such as a page with all its fields, is larger than the limit for imports, or the export contains more spaces than the limit. A space export contains one space.
xmlElementTooLarge.action: Export the space again. If a single page is that large, shorten it in Confluence first.

csvFieldTooLarge.what: The export contains a value that is too large
csvFieldTooLarge.cause: A field of a table in the export is larger than the limit for imports.
csvFieldTooLarge.action: Export the space again. If a single page is that large, shorten it in Confluence first.

csvRowTooLarge.what: The export contains a row that is too large
csvRowTooLarge.cause: A row of a table in the export is larger than the limit for imports.
csvRowTooLarge.action: Export the space again from Confluence.

csvTooManyFields.what: A table in the export has too many columns
csvTooManyFields.cause: Real exports have far fewer columns; the file may be damaged.
csvTooManyFields.action: Export the space again from Confluence.

csvUnterminatedQuote.what: A table in the export ends too early
csvUnterminatedQuote.action: Export the space again and upload the complete file.

keyTaken.cause: Another space got the key after the import was set up.
keyTaken.action: Start a new import with another key.

fileChanged.what: The file in the import folder changed
fileChanged.cause: It was replaced or changed after Lunedo read it.
fileChanged.action: Choose the file again so that Lunedo reads the new version.

fileMissing.cause: The import has no export file.
fileMissing.action: Choose the export file in the first step.

importFileUnavailable.what: The file is no longer in the import folder
importFileUnavailable.cause: It was moved or deleted, or it is not a regular file.
importFileUnavailable.action: Ask the person who runs the server to place the file there again, then choose it.

importFolderUnavailable.what: The import folder cannot be read
importFolderUnavailable.cause: The folder does not exist on the server or Lunedo has no access to it.
importFolderUnavailable.action: Ask the person who runs the server to check the import folder.

uploadIncomplete.cause: Some parts of the file have not arrived.
uploadIncomplete.action: Continue the upload in the first step.

storageFull.cause: The storage ran out of room while the import was writing files, so Lunedo stopped it.
storageFull.action: Ask the person who runs Lunedo to free up or add storage. Then discard this import and start it again.

organizationImportLimit.what: Import storage of the organization full
organizationImportLimit.cause: Uploaded exports and the data Lunedo read from them reached the limit for this organization while this export was being read.
organizationImportLimit.action: Delete drafts you no longer need, accept or discard finished imports, or ask the instance administrators to raise the limit. Then choose the file again.

internalError.what: The import stopped after several attempts
internalError.cause: An unexpected problem occurred again and again.
internalError.action: Discard the import and start it again. If it fails again, ask the person who runs the server to check the logs.

foreignSpace.what: This export is from another Confluence space
foreignSpace.cause: A re-import only accepts an export of the Confluence space this space was imported from.
foreignSpace.action: Choose an export of the same Confluence space, or start a new import into a new space.

noMarkdown.cause: The ZIP file contains no .md or .markdown files outside hidden folders.
noMarkdown.action: Pack the folder with the Markdown files into a ZIP file and upload it again.

macroDocument.cause: A document contains macros. Lunedo never runs or imports macros.
macroDocument.action: Open the document in Word, save it as .docx without macros and upload it again.

documentTooLarge.cause: A document is larger than 100 MB.
documentTooLarge.action: Remove large images or split the document, then upload it again.

unreadableDocument.cause: A file is damaged, encrypted, in the old .doc format or not a Word document.
unreadableDocument.action: Open the document in Word, save it as .docx without a password and upload it again.

selectionMissing.cause: The import does not know which space to read.
selectionMissing.action: Choose the space in the selection step.

connectionMissing.cause: Lunedo deleted the token of this import, or it was never entered.
connectionMissing.action: Test the connection again in the connection step.

confluenceUnauthorized.cause: The token is wrong, has expired or was revoked.
confluenceUnauthorized.action: Create a new token and test the connection again.

confluenceSpaceMissing.cause: The space was deleted or the token can no longer read it.
confluenceSpaceMissing.action: Choose another space, or use a token of an account that can read the space.

confluenceCertificate.cause: Confluence uses a certificate Lunedo does not trust.
confluenceCertificate.action: Add the certificate of the authority under Advanced in the connection step.

confluenceBlocked.cause: The address of Confluence is in a private network that Lunedo may not contact.
confluenceBlocked.action: Ask the instance administrators to allow this network for outgoing connections.

confluenceRedirect.cause: Confluence answered with a redirect to another address. Lunedo does not follow redirects.
confluenceRedirect.action: Enter the address Confluence really uses and test the connection again.

confluenceInvalidResponse.cause: Confluence sent an answer Lunedo cannot read, possibly from a proxy in between.
confluenceInvalidResponse.action: Check the address, then try again. If it keeps failing, use the XML export of the space.

confluenceResponseTooLarge.cause: A page or a list from Confluence is larger than Lunedo reads at once.
confluenceResponseTooLarge.action: Import the space through its XML export instead.

confluenceUnreachable.cause: Confluence did not answer, even after several attempts.
confluenceUnreachable.action: Check that Confluence is running and reachable, then start reading again.

confluenceRateLimited.what: Confluence keeps asking to slow down
confluenceRateLimited.cause: Confluence limited the requests for longer than Lunedo waits.
confluenceRateLimited.action: Try again later, for example outside office hours.

reasons.critical: {percent} used: uploads are refused. Free space or enlarge the volume now.

reasons.backlog: {queued, plural, one {# job is} other {# jobs are}} waiting. Check that the worker runs and is not overloaded.
reasons.unreachable: The job queue could not be read. Check the database connection and the worker's logs.

reasons.unavailable: The collaboration server does not answer, so nobody can edit. Check that it runs and LUNEDO_COLLAB_UPSTREAM.

maintenance.title: Maintenance mode
maintenance.description: Makes the instance read-only for scripted maintenance, for example an update or a data migration, with a message for everyone.

banner.title: Maintenance in progress
banner.readOnly: You can read and search, but changes are not saved until the maintenance ends.
banner.signInPaused: Signing in is paused for everyone except instance administrators.

state.title: State
state.label: Maintenance mode
state.signInPaused: Signing in is paused for everyone except instance administrators. Existing sessions stay signed in, read-only.

effects.title: What happens while it is on
effects.readOnly: Every change through the interface and the API is refused, also for instance administrators. Reading, search and exports of single pages keep working.
effects.editors: Open editors switch to read-only and show the message; they become editable again when maintenance ends, without reloading.
effects.jobs: Background jobs that change content, such as imports, copies and scheduled publications, wait and run afterwards.
effects.running: Backups, mail delivery, search indexing, SCIM and identity provider synchronization keep running, so access is still removed when someone leaves.
effects.sessions: Nobody is signed out. Switching on and off is recorded in the audit log and shown on the system status page.

form.title: Switch on
form.messageHint: Shown in the banner on every page and in knowledge base portals, for example when the maintenance ends. At most {max} characters.
form.messageTooLong: The message has {count} characters. Shorten it to at most {max}.
form.blockSignIn: Pause signing in for everyone except instance administrators
form.blockSignInHint: People who are signed in stay signed in, but can only read.
form.undoFailed: The previous state could not be restored
form.commandLine: Scripts switch it with ./lunedo maintenance on or off in the installation directory, or with the command lunedo maintenance in the container.

check.title: Update check
check.offByEnvironment: LUNEDO_UPDATE_CHECK=false turns the update check off completely; Lunedo makes no request for it. Remove the variable and restart to turn it on.
check.privacy: Once a day the worker downloads the public version file {url}. The request sends nothing about this instance.

failures.unreachable: The server of the version file could not be reached. Check the network and LUNEDO_UPDATE_CHECK_URL; Lunedo tries again tomorrow.
failures.timeout: The version file did not arrive within 15 seconds. Check the network; Lunedo tries again tomorrow.
failures.blockedAddress: The address of the version file is in a private network. List it in LUNEDO_OUTBOUND_ALLOWED_NETWORKS or use a public mirror.
failures.insecureAddress: Public addresses of the version file must use HTTPS. Change LUNEDO_UPDATE_CHECK_URL.
failures.untrustedCertificate: The certificate of the server is not trusted. Check the mirror's certificate.
failures.tooManyRedirects: The server redirected too often. Check LUNEDO_UPDATE_CHECK_URL.
failures.httpStatus: The server answered with an error, for example because the file does not exist there yet. Check LUNEDO_UPDATE_CHECK_URL; Lunedo tries again tomorrow.
failures.tooLarge: The version file is larger than 2 MB, so it is not a Lunedo version file. Check LUNEDO_UPDATE_CHECK_URL.
failures.invalidFile: The file is not a Lunedo version file. Check LUNEDO_UPDATE_CHECK_URL.
